mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically over the last three weeks (-71.4 to -65.4), indicating a steady reopening trend that will continue to lift retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks as consumers resume discretionary outings.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -71.4 to -65.4 over the last three weeks
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean over the last 28 days, reversing the established upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has improved from -63.9 to -60.6 over the snapshot window, reflecting increased willingness to travel; since transit use is a precondition for reaching retail destinations, continued transit recovery will drive RETAIL_REC higher over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -63.9 to -60.6 across the four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 2 weeks despite TRANSIT continuing to improve week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility remains elevated and stable near +16 to +17 percent, indicating persistent home-centered behavior; if RESIDENTIAL spikes above 18 points in any week, this signals a behavioral retrenchment that will suppress RETAIL_REC over the following week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above 18.0 percent in a weekly mean
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL has ranged 16.0-17.4 over the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline the week following a RESIDENTIAL reading above 18.0, or RESIDENTIAL never crosses that threshold yet RETAIL_REC still falls.

mechanism_narrative: Joint improvement in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility together reflects a compounding return of daytime urban activity (commuting plus errands), which has a stronger positive effect on RETAIL_REC than either series alone, driving retail mobility higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT show net improvement over the four-week window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise even when both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improve concurrently for two or more consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility declined from t-2w (-29.6) to t-1w (-31.3) before partially recovering to -29.3 at t-0w, suggesting outdoor recreation substitution; if PARKS continues to recover alongside flat GROCERY_PHARM, combined outdoor and errand activity will push RETAIL_REC upward over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises for two consecutive weeks while GROCERY_PHARM stays within +/-2 points
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS recovered from -31.3 to -29.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 2 weeks despite PARKS rising two consecutive weeks and GROCERY_PHARM remaining flat.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility drops sharply (more than 5 points week-on-week) from its current level near -53, this would signal a tightening of reopening policy or a new restriction regime, which will suppress RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks as reduced commuting curtails downstream retail trips.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES has oscillated between -52.6 and -55.6 over the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 4 weeks following a WORKPLACES drop exceeding 5 points in a single week.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-July represents peak summer season in Manhattan; under a steady-state reopening regime without new restrictions, seasonal outdoor and leisure demand will sustain a gradual upward drift in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks independent of short-term fluctuations in other series.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC trends flat or downward over the next 4 weeks despite no new restrictive policy signals appearing in WORKPLACES or TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in TRANSIT use and fall in RESIDENTIAL time indicates a behavioral shift away from home-bound caution toward venturing out; when both conditions co-occur within the same week, this combination predicts an accelerated rise in RETAIL_REC over the following week more strongly than either signal alone.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises and RESIDENTIAL falls in the same week relative to the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved to -60.6 while RESIDENTIAL eased to 16.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise the week following a joint TRANSIT increase and RESIDENTIAL decrease relative to the prior week.
